summary:
"SPHEREx SkyTime" is an interactive astronomical data explorer developed to make NASA’s SPHEREx observations easier to access, explore, and understand. Users can explore the sky using celestial coordinates and visualize spectral data across SPHEREx’s six detector bands (D1–D6).

The application addresses the challenge of accessing and interpreting large astronomical datasets by bringing data retrieval and visualization into one interface. It uses SPHEREx spectral-image exposures from NASA/IPAC IRSA’s SIA2 service as its primary data source, with the SPHEREx DR1 All-Sky Spectral Cube hosted through IRSA/AWS Open Data as an automatic fallback when the primary service is unavailable.

By making scientific data more accessible and interactive, SkyTime helps users explore the infrared universe, understand spectral variations across wavelengths, and engage with real astronomical observations rather than static representations.
details:
Project Details – SPHEREx SkyTime

SPHEREx SkyTime is an interactive web-based astronomical data explorer that allows users to explore real infrared observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission. Users can search for celestial objects or enter their Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates, specify a search radius, and retrieve available observations for that region of the sky.

The application retrieves individual SPHEREx spectral-image exposures through NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA)'s SIA2 service. When this primary service is unavailable, it automatically switches to the SPHEREx DR1 All-Sky Spectral Cube hosted through IRSA/AWS Open Data, ensuring that users can still explore spectral information. Retrieved FITS data is processed on the backend to generate visual representations and scientific measurements. Users can explore observations across the six SPHEREx detector bands (D1–D6), inspect spectral and photometric information, view observations on an interactive sky map, and explore available observations chronologically. The interface also provides visualization controls such as image stretching, colour maps, zodiacal-light subtraction, and comparison views.

The project makes complex astronomical datasets easier to access and interpret by combining data retrieval, scientific processing, and interactive visualization in one platform. Instead of requiring users to work directly with raw astronomical files and specialized tools, SkyTime provides a more approachable way to investigate infrared observations. Its intended impact is to encourage curiosity about the infrared universe, support astronomy education, and make publicly available scientific data more accessible to students, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts.

Technology and tools used: The frontend was developed using React, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, with Vite for development and building. The backend uses Node.js and Express to handle archive requests, FITS processing, and API endpoints. Aladin Lite powers the interactive astronomical sky viewer. The project integrates NASA/IPAC IRSA's SIA2 service and the SPHEREx DR1 All-Sky Spectral Cube through IRSA/AWS Open Data. It was developed using standard web-development tools and deployed using Netlify for the frontend and Render for the backend.

Creativity and design considerations: The central idea behind SkyTime is to turn astronomical observations into an interactive exploration experience rather than simply displaying static images. The application combines a sky viewer, observation explorer, scientific measurements, and chronological visualization in a single workflow. During development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessibility of public datasets, reliability when external archive services become unavailable, performance when processing large FITS files, and clarity when presenting scientific information. The automatic fallback mechanism is particularly important because it allows the application to remain useful even when its primary data service experiences interruptions.
